title: Feature-prefixed undeclared secret keys are not deletable
detail: The delete handler still accepts legacy undeclared keys, but a key starting with "<feature>:" of a mounted feature now fails as unknown key. Feature-owned credentials keep their writeRoles protection.

title: createSecretsFeature carries its env schema type
detail: createSecretsFeature returns the feature typed with secretsEnvSchema, so composeEnvSchema types the KUMIKO_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY_* variables.

title: secrets exports SecretsHandlers (set, delete) and SecretsQueries (list) handler names
detail: Apps dispatch secrets:write:set, secrets:write:delete and the list query through the exported constants like ConfigHandlers, instead of string literals.

title: secrets:write:set and secrets:write:delete join the request transaction
detail: Both handlers ran on the boot database connection, so in an /api/batch a later failing command rolled back the config writes but kept the stored secret. They now run on the request transaction (escape hatch unsafeRaw, reason documented on the handler), so a batch of config and secret writes is stored as a whole or not at all.

title: secrets delete no longer requires a declared key
detail: secrets:write:delete used to answer 404 unknownKey for a key that no feature declares, so a row stored before the declaration gate existed could never be removed. Delete now skips the declaration check; writeRoles of a declared key or namespace still apply, and set keeps the gate.

title: SecretsContext.withRunner(tx) runs secret access on a given transaction
detail: The OAuth refresh now reads and writes the refresh token on its advisory-lock transaction, so a refresh holds one pool connection instead of two and parallel refreshes cannot starve the pool. Custom SecretsContext implementations need a `withRunner` method.

title: Recognise the invalid-secret-value error
detail: `secrets` exports `isInvalidSecretValueError`, which recognises the validation error that `secrets:write:set` and `ctx.secrets.set` raise when a value fails the key's `valueSchema`. It also exports `SECRETS_ERROR_KEYS` (the i18n keys of the secrets write errors) and `INVALID_SECRET_VALUE_CODE` (the field error code), so callers can map the failure to their own message instead of matching strings.

title: Chat channel secret values are validated on write
detail:
`r.secret` and `r.secretNamespace` accept a `valueSchema`. `secrets:write:set` checks the value against it after the key and role checks and answers a failure with a 400 validation error on field `value` (`secrets.errors.invalidValue`); the response never contains the value or the schema's issues. `secrets:write:delete` is unaffected.
The chat channels use it: Slack, Discord and Teams webhook secrets must be URLs that pass the channel's host allowlist (including the Discord `/api/webhooks/` path), and the Telegram bot token must have the `<bot id>:<secret>` shape. The allowlist comes from the same options as the channel, so `createChannelSlackFeature({ allowedHosts })` also governs what can be stored.
`channel-slack`, `channel-discord`, `channel-teams` and `channel-telegram` now export their secret keys (`SLACK_SECRET_KEYS`, `DISCORD_SECRET_KEYS`, `TEAMS_SECRET_KEYS`, `TELEGRAM_SECRET_KEYS`), allowlist constants and `isTelegramChatId` / `isTelegramBotToken`. `delivery` exports `checkChatWebhookTarget`, `chatWebhookUrlSchema` and `resolveChatWebhookTarget`, so apps can validate an address or URL when a user creates a channel.
Existing invalid secrets stay stored; only new writes are checked. Writes through `ctx.secrets.set` in feature code run through the same check.

title: ctx.secrets.set validates against the declared valueSchema
migration: Code that calls createSecretsContext({ db, masterKeyProvider }) must also pass registry (the booted Registry). Programmatic ctx.secrets.set calls with a value that fails the key's valueSchema now throw a ValidationError instead of storing it.

title: secrets:set and secrets:delete accept only keys declared via r.secret; r.secret takes writeRoles
detail: Both handlers reject a key that no feature declared with `r.secret` (404, i18n key `secrets.errors.unknownKey`). `r.secret` takes `writeRoles`: when set, only users holding one of those roles may set or delete that key (403, i18n key `secrets.errors.writeDenied`). The roles narrow the handler access, so both checks must pass. An empty `writeRoles` array throws at declaration.
migration: Declare every key you set through `secrets:write:set` via `r.secret`. Rows stored under undeclared keys stay in the table but can no longer be set or deleted through the API. A key that only SystemAdmin may write declares `writeRoles: ["SystemAdmin"]`, and the secrets feature must then grant SystemAdmin handler access via `createSecretsFeature({ roles: ["TenantAdmin", "SystemAdmin"] })`. Tests that set a key no feature declares need the same fix: the kumiko-studio test `bundled-stack.integration.test.ts` sets `ai-foundation:secret:anthropic-api-key`, which no feature declares; kumiko-ai-foundation 0.39.1 and 0.40.1 declare the Anthropic key as `ai-provider-anthropic:secret:anthropic-api-key`.

title: createSecretsFeature rejects access and roles together
detail: `createSecretsFeature` throws at mount when both `access` and `roles` are passed; `access` used to silently discard `roles`. The personal-access-token mint form builds its i18n keys from the shared key helpers, and `ACTION_FORM_ENTITY` is now exported from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/ui-types`. The rate-limiting feature registers de/en copy for its error keys.
migration: Remove `roles` from the `createSecretsFeature` options when `access` is set (or drop `access` and keep `roles`). Before, `roles` was silently ignored next to `access`.

title: rotateJob takes the raw DbConnection as a third argument; the rotate job declares escapeHatch (fw#2914).
detail: JobContext.db is now a tenant-filtered TenantDb. Rotation re-encrypts every tenant's secrets, so the `rotate` registration declares `escapeHatch` and passes `ctx.db.unsafeRaw(reason)` to `rotateJob(payload, ctx, db)`.
migration: Direct callers of the exported `rotateJob` pass the raw `DbConnection` as the third argument. Apps that only mount the feature need no change.

title: derivePurposeSecret: HKDF-based per-purpose secret derivation (fw#1623).
detail: Previously copy-pasted in four apps as deriveSubSecret. The second parameter is a domain separator, not a label — the rename says so. auth-mfa gains resolveMfaTokenSecrets, which owns the two MFA purpose strings so a prod and a dev entrypoint cannot drift apart and invalidate each other's tokens.
